key_insight: Phonon Fine-Tuning (PFT) improves ML interatomic potentials by directly supervising second-order force constants: matching the MLIP energy Hessian to DFT-computed force constants corrects curvature errors and greatly improves vibrational/phonon predictions.
problem_solved: Standard MLIP training on energies, forces, and stresses often yields incorrect curvature (second derivatives) of the potential energy surface, causing poor predictions of vibrational properties (phonons, vibrational density of states, thermal behavior).
method: Compute DFT force constants via finite-displacement calculations to obtain target second-order derivatives (force constant matrix).
Evaluate the MLIP energy Hessian (analytic or finite-difference) and add a Hessian/force-constant matching loss to fine-tune a pretrained MLIP.
Fine-tune with a multi-term loss to preserve original energy/force/stress accuracy while correcting curvature for improved phonon predictions.
impact: PFT gives ML/Materials practitioners a lightweight, targeted way to fix curvature deficiencies in MLIPs, enabling reliable prediction of vibrational and thermal properties and more stable atomistic dynamics without full retraining.
visual_elements: Schematic energy vs. displacement curve showing curvature mismatch: baseline MLIP vs. PFT-corrected MLIP vs. DFT reference.
Pipeline flowchart: DFT finite displacements → force constants (target Hessian) → MLIP Hessian computation → PFT loss → fine-tuned MLIP.
Before/after phonon dispersion or vibrational density-of-states plots highlighting improved agreement with DFT after PFT.
Bar/line chart comparing second-derivative (Hessian) errors and resulting property errors (e.g., phonon frequencies, specific heat) for baseline vs. PFT.
paper_title: PFT: Phonon Fine-tuning for Machine Learned Interatomic Potentials
paper_authors: Teddy Koker, Abhijeet Gangan, Mit Kotak, Jaime Marian, Tess Smidt
